newsitem.title: USA: Forrester sees Internet commerce growth.
newsitem.headline: Forrester sees Internet commerce growth.

text.p: Forrester Research Inc predicted on Monday that the market for Internet commerce software would reach $3.2 billion by the year 2000, after totaling only $22.4 million in 1996.

"Consumer-oriented commerce is where the market hype was in 1996, but it won't have nearly as much of an effect on the industry in the next couple of years as buiness-to-business commerce," said Stan Dolberg, Forrester director of sofware strategies, in a statement.
Forrester cited aggressive pricing, improved services and increased activity from mid-sized firms as key factors in the predicted 60-fold increase in corporate Internet commerce spending.
Forrester said merchant servers will have to become more flexible to handle business-to-business commerce.
The research company also predicts a shakeout, with smaller players in the Internet commerce software market being driven into vertical and niche applications.
